ThingDef.label: agent orange canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of agent orange. Load it into a agent orange vent, or use it to make agent orange traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

A jungle-war defoliant, named for the orange band painted on its drums. Farmers clear fields with it; soldiers strip the brush that raiders hide in and the dry grass that carries fire up to the walls. What it leaves in the body stays for years.

- Grass, bushes, crops and flowers wither and die within a few seconds.
- Trees drop their leaves at once but only die after two to three minutes in thick mist.
- Trees with special powers (anima, gauranlen and the like) are spared.
- Mildly toxic: a minute in thick mist gives people and animals light toxic buildup, small animals a little more. Toxic buildup lingers for days and, built up over many exposures, can bring dementia or cancer.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely; toxic resistance reduces the dose.

Lethality 0.5/5. Complexity 1/5. Research: agrochemical aerosols.

ThingDef.description:

ThingDef.label: verminbane canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of verminbane. Load it into a verminbane vent, or use it to make verminbane traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Nicotine salts and cheap nerve poisons, sold by the drum to farms plagued by rats and megascarabs. Every breath carries the same dose; a small body just has less room for it.

Living creatures only. The smaller the body, the faster it works.
- Rats, squirrels and other vermin die within a few seconds, megascarabs and other small insects within about five.
- Cats and dogs sicken over a minute or two; megaspiders and other big insects die in about forty seconds.
- People get nausea and tremors in the first minute and convulsions in the second; about three minutes in thick fog can kill.
- Muffalo and other large animals barely notice.
- Its rat-poison blood thinner makes every wound bleed harder for days. After about 40 seconds in thick fog the body starts bleeding inside 2-4 hours later, and keeps bleeding until a doctor treats it.
- Insect hives in the fog slowly die.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely. General toxin resistance doesn't help; it is made for creatures that shrug off other poisons.

Lethality 1/5, 5/5 against vermin. Complexity 1/5. Research: agrochemical aerosols.

ThingDef.label: barbsmoke canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of barbsmoke. Load it into a barbsmoke vent, or use it to make barbsmoke traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Microscopic crystalline barbs carried in a pink-grey haze. It is not breathed: the barbs work into the skin through seams, cuffs and collars and set off every nerve they touch.

- Pain spikes within a second; most pawns drop into pain shock.
- Movement is capped at 30% and manipulation at 20% while the spasms last.
- Chemical burns on the limbs, hands and neck that can blister and turn septic.
Gas masks do nothing. Only a sealed suit that covers torso and legs and protects against toxins (such as a chemical protection suit) keeps it out.

Lethality 2/5. Complexity 3/5. Research: weaponized gas.

ThingDef.label: dreadspore vapor canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of dreadspore vapor. Load it into a dreadspore vapor vent, or use it to make dreadspore vapor traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Spores of a cave fungus, bred until a few breaths flood the brain with terror. It does no harm by itself; the harm comes from the people breathing it.

Living creatures only.
- Shooting accuracy drops by 80% at once.
- After about 6 seconds the mind snaps, whatever the mood: brawlers, bloodlusters and psychopaths go berserk and attack whoever is closest; everyone else drops what they carry and flees.
- No lasting harm once it wears off.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely.

Lethality 1.5/5. Complexity 3/5. Research: weaponized gas.

ThingDef.label: gear-rot fume canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of gear-rot fume. Load it into a gear-rot fume vent, or use it to make gear-rot fume traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

The answer to raiders who stroll through gas lines behind sealed masks. Gear-rot ignores the wearer and eats the kit: fabric, polymer, ceramic plate and steel pit and crumble in minutes.

- In thick fume, every worn item loses 2-5% of its hit points per second.
- Masks, helmets and armor that reach zero fall apart, leaving the wearer open to whatever else is in the air.
- Uncovered skin takes acid burns.
Mix it with a lethal gas.

Lethality 3/5. Complexity 4/5. Research: corrosive agents.

ThingDef.label: scourge fog canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of scourge fog. Load it into a scourge fog vent, or use it to make scourge fog traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

A heavy, clinging acid for ground you never want back. Nothing worth salvaging survives where it settles, and it does not care what you are wearing.

- Kills every plant it touches: crops, grass and trees.
- Dissolves weapons, apparel, corpses and resources lying on the ground.
- Eats doors, barricades, traps, conduits and walls. Wood goes in seconds, steel in under a minute, stone and plasteel hold out far longer.
- Burns skin straight through ordinary clothes and armor. A gas mask shields only the face and lungs; a chemical suit only the body. Only both together keep it off.
- Breathed without a mask it burns the lungs. Half a minute in thick fog and the lungs fill with fluid over the next hours: fatal unless a doctor treats it. Badly burned lungs scar for good.
Raiders path around scourge fog unless sapping orders drive them through.

Lethality 2.5/5. Complexity 4/5. Research: corrosive agents.

ThingDef.label: slumbercloud canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of slumbercloud. Load it into a slumbercloud vent, or use it to make slumbercloud traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

A fast sedative aerosol from colonial police stocks. It takes the fight out of a room without leaving bodies to bury.

Living creatures only.
- About 4 seconds: the pawn collapses into a deep sleep and drops its weapon.
- Carried into clean air, they wake several hours later with no lasting harm. Ideal for taking prisoners and harvesting bionics.
- Left lying in thick cloud for 8 seconds, the sleep becomes an anoxic coma that kills after 10 more seconds. Pulled out of the coma alive, the pawn keeps brain scarring.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely; toxic resistance reduces the dose.

Lethality 3.5/5. Complexity 2/5. Research: sedative aerosols.

ThingDef.label: hexvein mist canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of hexvein mist. Load it into a hexvein mist vent, or use it to make hexvein mist traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Named for the black, branching bruises it leaves under the skin. Hexvein jams the junctions between nerve and muscle in anything with a nervous system: people, animals and insectoids alike.

Living creatures only; mechanoids are immune.
- About 3 seconds: tremors (aiming delay +150%, movement -40%).
- About 6 seconds: convulsions, vomiting, extreme pain, no manipulation.
- 10 to 12 seconds: the breathing muscles stop.
- Survivors suffer 15 to 30 days of neuro-ataxia. Those who went through convulsions keep permanent nerve damage.
It soaks through skin as well as lungs: a gas mask alone only slows it to about half a minute. A chemical suit and a gas mask together stop it.

Lethality 4.5/5. Complexity 2/5. Research: nerve agents.

ThingDef.label: deathbreath fog canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of deathbreath fog. Load it into a deathbreath fog vent, or use it to make deathbreath fog traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Developed for trench wars on a world with nobody left to remember them. An odourless asphyxiant that shuts a body down in stages: the brain, then the lungs, then the heart.

Living creatures only; mechanoids are immune.
- About 2 seconds in dense fog: collapse.
- About 5 seconds: respiratory and cardiac arrest.
- Pawns pulled out right after collapsing live, but usually with hypoxic brain scarring or myocardial necrosis that only glitterworld surgery, a biosculpter or a healer mech serum can repair.
- After about 3 seconds the dose is lethal: deathbreath poisoning keeps spreading after the pawn is out and kills within hours unless a doctor treats it.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely; toxic resistance reduces the dose.

Lethality 5/5. Complexity 2/5. Research: terminal asphyxiants.

ThingDef.label: aegis swarm canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of aegis swarm. Load it into a aegis swarm vent, or use it to make aegis swarm traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

Not a gas at all but billions of drifting micro-drones keyed to faction transponders. Safe to vent into your own corridors during a breach.

- Colonists, allies, neutral visitors and tame animals are recognized and left alone.
- Anything hostile is sliced across its outer body: heavy bleeding, pain, slowed movement. Some drones slip through the cuts to the lungs, liver, kidneys and stomach, and those wounds bleed inside.
- Gas masks and toxic resistance give no protection; armor does.
- Downed enemies are left alone, so prisoners can be taken.

Lethality 3.5/5. Complexity 4/5. Research: IFF nanite swarms.

ThingDef.label: cypherphage cloud canister
ThingDef.description:
A pressurized canister of cypherphage cloud. Load it into a cypherphage cloud vent, or use it to make cypherphage cloud traps, grenades and shells. It bursts if destroyed.

A nanite plague for mechanoid logic cores. It rewrites firmware at random, and now and then the result is loyal.

Mechanoids only; harmless to living creatures.
Every 3 seconds a mechanoid spends in thick cloud, it rolls one malfunction:
- 40% loop stun for 4-6 seconds
- 25% component meltdown: fire, and a ruptured reprocessor that leaks chemfuel and explodes when the mechanoid dies
- 20% sensors blind for 15 seconds
- 10% permanent subroutine scramble: it attacks everything around it
- 5% firmware hijack: the mechanoid joins your colony

Lethality 4/5 against mechanoids, 0/5 against the living. Complexity 5/5. Research: cypherphage nanites.
